newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: STEEL COMMITTEE TO LOOK FOR NEW INDUSTRY ENTRANTS

A member of the Federal parliamentary committee reviewing the steel industry says with BHP announcing its steel plan, the committee will now look for other potential players to enter the steel industry.
Committee member, M-P Bob Baldwin says BHP's announcement it intends to shutdown its steelmaking operation in Newcastle will only marginally affect the work of the bi-paritsan steel committee.
He says the committee will still make its report on the steel industry, but will be looking to other industry players to step in where BHP has pulled out.
The committee's report is expected to be released later this month.
CLAIMS OF RIGGED CASINO WHEEL REJECTED BY CROWN
Crown Casino in Melbourne has described as ridiculous and bizarre, a claim that a promotional gaming wheel has been rigged.
The claim is being investigated by Victoria's Casino and Gaming Authority.
The wheel has been seized by officers from the Police Gaming Squad, after a complaint that it was doctored so it wouldn't land on the major prize of 25-thousand dollars.
The complaint is believed to have come from a contestant who spun the wheel in a weekly promotion for a Melbourne radio station.
Crown spokesman Gary O'Neil says the publicity generated by the promotion would more than cover the 25-thousand-dollar value of the major prize, and he described the rigging allegation as bizarre.

A spokesman for the Radio Station involved in the promotion, 3AW, says the sataion has complete faith in Crown's integrity, and if there was a malfunction in the wheel, it would be a maintenance problem, and not an attempt to manipulate the outcome.
JUDGE DESCRIBES 1960S POLICY AS GENOCIDE
The head of the inquiry into the stolen Aboriginal generation, has described the policy of taking children from their families as genocide.
Former High Court Judge, Sir Ronald Wilson, has also apologised for his personal role in the policy.
Part of Sir Ronald's job in the Presbyterian Church in the 1960s was to oversee the council which ran Sister Kate's home in WA which took some of Australia's 30-thousand stolen children.
Sir Ronald is now the President of the Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission, and sat on the inquiry into the stolen generation.
He admitted his deep sorrow for the role both he and the church played in the policy.
VIC PUBLIC SERVANTS TO WALK OFF JOB TODAY
Thousands of Commonwealth public servants will walk off the job across Victoria this afternoon, in a dispute over employment conditions.
They're angry at the Government's decision to rule out funding for any future pay rises, saying it will lead to further job losses and cuts to services.
They're also concerned long-held employment conditions could be lost.
The Community and Public Sector Union expects the two hour afternoon stoppage will affect all Federal Government agencies in the state, including Social Security, Customs, CES and the Tax Office.
Meanwhile, disability groups are taking what they describe as an unprecedented national protest against planned Federal budget cuts.
Peak bodies, representing consumer and service groups, are joining local representatives in rallies, planned today in all capital cities.
DECISION ON ASYLUM-SEEKERS EXPECTED TODAY
In what's being hailed as a test case for more than one-thousand East Timorese asylum-seekers, the Federal Court will today deliver its judgement on one man hoping for refugee status in Australia.
24 year old Kim Ko Jong appealed to the Court against a Refugee Review Tribunal decision that he's entitled to citizenship of East Timor's former colonial ruler, Portugal.
His application to the Immigration Department for refugee status in Australia was rejected following his arrival after the Dili massacre in East Timor in 1991.
The Federal Court ruling is expected to determine the future of 13-hundred other East Timorese, who've similarly applied for refugee status in Australia.
ARKELL CHARGED OVER CHILD SEX OFFENCES
Former Wollongong politician, Frank Arkell, has been charged with 29 sex offences against children, allegedly committed over a number of years.

The 67 year old former State Member and Lord Mayor of Wollongong, was taken into custody late yesterday, after being interviewed for several hours at his home by detectives from the State's Child Protection Enforcement Agency.
MASS MEETING OF NEWCASTLE STEELWORKERS
A mass meeting of Newcastle Steelworks employees this morning could signal the start of a national industrial campaign across all BHP sectors.
At this morning's meeting, unions will seek support for a campaign which is likely to involve other BHP steel centres, iron ore miners, coal miners and oil industry workers.
The results of the meeting will be taken to a meeting of the ACTU executive next Monday.
